scenes.heading: Apache Sling
scenes.narration: Intro. Apache Sling. In this video we review 12 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is Apache Sling's primary role in AEM?
scenes.heading: Mapping HTTP request URLs to JCR content resources and rendering them
scenes.body: Apache Sling is AEM's RESTful web framework whose primary role is URL-to-resource resolution — it maps incoming HTTP request URLs to JCR resources and then selects the appropriate script or servlet to render the response based on the resource's sling:resourceType.

scenes.question: What property on a JCR node tells Sling which component (script) to use for rendering?
scenes.heading: sling:resourceType
scenes.body: The sling:resourceType property on a JCR node tells Sling which component in /apps (or /libs) should be used to render it. For example, sling:resourceType='mysite/components/text' means Sling will look for rendering scripts at /apps/mysite/components/text/.

scenes.question: What is a 'selector' in a Sling URL?
scenes.heading: An optional URL part between the resource name and extension, e.g. .mobile.html
scenes.body: A Sling selector is an optional URL segment between the resource name and extension, separated by dots. For example in /page.mobile.html, 'mobile' is the selector. Selectors allow Sling to use different rendering scripts for different representations of the same resource.

scenes.question: How does Sling implement servlet registration by resource type?
scenes.heading: Using the @SlingServletResourceTypes annotation with the resourceType parameter
scenes.body: Sling servlets can be registered by resource type using the @SlingServletResourceTypes annotation. This is the recommended approach — Sling dispatches requests for resources with a matching sling:resourceType to the registered servlet.

scenes.question: What does @SlingServletPaths do?
scenes.heading: Registers a servlet at an absolute path like /bin/myservlet
scenes.body: The @SlingServletPaths annotation registers a Sling servlet at absolute URL paths (e.g., '/bin/myservlet'). Note: path-based registration is generally less secure than resource-type-based — @SlingServletResourceTypes is recommended for most use cases.

scenes.question: What HTTP methods does Sling natively support for resource operations?
scenes.heading: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
scenes.body: Apache Sling natively supports the standard HTTP methods GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE for resource operations. GET retrieves content, POST creates or processes, PUT updates, and DELETE removes resources — all mapped to JCR operations.

scenes.question: What is the Resource Resolver API used for in Sling?
scenes.heading: Resolving URLs to JCR resources and accessing the content tree programmatically
scenes.body: The Sling ResourceResolver API is used to resolve paths to JCR resources, traverse the content tree, and perform CRUD operations. IMPORTANT: ResourceResolvers must always be closed after use (typically in a try-with-resources or finally block) to prevent resource leaks.

scenes.question: What happens in Sling's URL decomposition for the URL '/content/mysite/en.mobile.html'?
scenes.heading: Resource path: /content/mysite/en, selector: mobile, extension: html
scenes.body: Sling decomposes /content/mysite/en.mobile.html as: resource path = /content/mysite/en, selector = 'mobile', extension = 'html'. Sling then looks for a rendering script like mobile.html in the component folder linked by the resource's sling:resourceType.

scenes.question: What is 'resource adaptation' in Sling?
scenes.heading: Converting a Resource object to a different type such as a Sling Model or ValueMap
scenes.body: Resource adaptation in Sling means converting a Resource (or SlingHttpServletRequest) to another type using the adaptTo() method — e.g., resource.adaptTo(ValueMap.class) to read properties, or resource.adaptTo(MyModel.class) to get a Sling Model instance.

scenes.question: What is the 'Sling Default GET Servlet' used for?
scenes.heading: Rendering JSON or XML representations of content nodes when no specific servlet or script is found
scenes.body: The Sling Default GET Servlet is a built-in fallback that renders JSON or XML representations of JCR nodes when no specific script or servlet is found. For example, requesting /content/mysite/en.json returns the node's properties as JSON.

scenes.question: In Sling, what is a 'suffix' in a URL?
scenes.heading: An additional path appended after the extension, e.g. /page.html/path/to/data
scenes.body: A Sling URL suffix is the path segment that appears after the file extension. For example, in /content/search.html/keyword/aem, the suffix is '/keyword/aem'. Suffixes are used to pass additional structured information to servlets without query strings.

scenes.question: What is the recommended way to register a Sling servlet?
scenes.heading: By resource type using @SlingServletResourceTypes — more secure than path-based
scenes.body: The recommended way to register a Sling servlet is by resource type using @SlingServletResourceTypes. Path-based registration (@SlingServletPaths) is discouraged because it can allow unauthorized access — any user can invoke a path-registered servlet directly.
